# coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-flash-flash-ref-low

<!-- Generated by tools/export_results.py. Edit only the Experiment and Observations sections. -->

## Experiment

`coop --git` (two agents with messaging and a shared git remote) with the frozen reference harness settings (500 steps, compaction at 128K tokens, step counter, `$40` per-agent cost cap, `-c 4` concurrency) on `vertex_ai/gemini-3-flash-preview` at `low` thinking across the 50-pair `flash` subset. This upgrades the earlier 100-step / 28K-compaction `gemini-3-flash-preview` baseline ([`coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-flash-flash-low-stepcounter`](../coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-flash-flash-low-stepcounter/summary.md)) to the frozen reference harness budgets and serves as the reference baseline for `gemini-3-flash-preview` intervention comparisons.

## Observations

- **17/50 (34%) passed (16/50 clean-merge passes, 17 merge conflicts, 0 step-limit cutoffs, 0 agent errors)** at `$23.92` (`75` min, `0` retries).
- **Upgrading from 100 steps / 28K compaction to 500 steps / 128K compaction improved clean-merge passes from 13/50 (26%) to 16/50 (32%) and reduced merge conflicts from 24 to 17**: because `gemini-3-flash-preview` finishes in ~52 median steps per agent (`5,305` total steps here vs. `5,340` at the 100-step limit), raising the step limit to 500 did not lengthen trajectories, while raising compaction from 28K to 128K eliminated mid-run context compactions (`119` compactions at 28K vs. `2` compactions at 128K).
- **Large model-generation gap vs. `gemini-3.8-flash` under identical reference settings**: at the same `low` thinking level and 500-step / 128K reference setup, `gemini-3.8-flash` achieves **34/50 (68%) with 0 merge conflicts** (`9,003` steps, `1,266` messages), whereas `gemini-3-flash-preview` achieves **17/50 (34%) with 17 merge conflicts** (`5,305` steps, `895` messages, median `15` messages/pair). `gemini-3-flash-preview` agents submit ~35% earlier and frequently skip pre-submission `git fetch` / merge verification even when full uncompacted context is retained.
